mainTopic: Marriage and the harsh rhetoric about the עם הארץ; then the minimum amounts for returning sacrificial meat compared with זימון
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא's image: a match between a Torah family and an עם הארץ family does not take hold. A new ברייתא ranks the best families to marry into, starting with the daughter of a תלמיד חכם, and warns against marrying into an עם הארץ family. The גמרא then brings a series of very harsh statements from רבי, רבי אלעזר, רבי יוחנן, רבי עקיבא, רבי מאיר, רבי אליעזר and רבי חייא about the bitter hostility between עמי הארץ and תלמידי חכמים. These statements are deliberate exaggeration aimed at people who were openly hostile to Torah, not practical halacha. A ברייתא then gives six practical rules of caution with an עם הארץ, and a יש אומרים adds that we do not announce his lost item. The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא disagrees because righteous descendants may inherit the item. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה about someone who left Jerusalem with sacrificial meat. It raises a contradiction with the amounts רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה give for זימון. רבי יוחנן switches the names, while אביי explains that one dispute rests on פסוקים and the other on סברא. רבי יהודה's reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the grapevine metaphor
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the previous ברייתא: a match with an עם הארץ family is unfitting and does not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and it does not take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that began on the previous lines. That ברייתא compared a Torah scholar marrying into an עם הארץ family to vine grapes mixed with thornbush grapes, something 'ugly and unacceptable.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא said that a Torah family joined with a Torah family is like vine grapes with vine grapes: beautiful, and it takes hold. The opposite pairing is described here as something that 'does not take hold,' meaning the two do not blend well. This word ends that metaphor.

keyTerms.meaning: Accepted; takes hold (like a successful graft)

phrases.english: and it is not accepted (does not take hold).
phrases.notes: This finishes the saying 'דבר כעור ואינו מתקבל': an ugly thing that just doesn't take hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינוֹ מִתְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A match between a Torah home and an עם הארץ home is pictured as a mismatch that does not take hold.

steps.title: The ladder of preferred families to marry into
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא ranks which families a person should seek to marry into, starting with the daughter of a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A person should always sell everything he owns to marry the daughter of a Torah scholar. If he can't find one, he should marry the daughter of one of the great people of the generation. If not, the daughter of a community head. If not, the daughter of a charity collector. If not, the daughter of a schoolteacher of children.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא gives a step-by-step list of the best families to marry into. The top choice is the family of a תלמיד חכם, and the list goes down level by level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ranking follows closeness to Torah and to serving the community. First comes a תלמיד חכם, then pious great people (גדולי הדור), then community heads, then those who handle צדקה, then teachers of children. Each level still values Torah and good deeds. Saying 'sell everything he owns' shows how highly this is valued.

keyTerms.meaning: Heads of the congregations / communal leaders

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is often quoted as the source for valuing a Torah home when choosing a שידוך.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should always sell all that he has,
and marry the daughter of a Torah scholar.
If he did not find the daughter of a Torah scholar,
he should marry the daughter of the great ones of the generation.
If he did not find the daughter of the great ones of the generation,
he should marry the daughter of the heads of congregations.
If he did not find the daughter of the heads of congregations,
he should marry the daughter of the charity collectors.
If he did not find the daughter of the charity collectors,
he should marry the daughter of the teachers of children.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְעוֹלָם יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on the same theme of marriage and Torah families.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should go to great lengths to marry into a Torah family, following a ranked order of preference.

steps.title: Warning against marrying into an עם הארץ family
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא warns against marrying the daughter of an עם הארץ, using very harsh imagery.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he should not marry the daughter of ignoramuses, because they are like disgusting creatures, their wives are like creeping things, and about their daughters the verse says: 'Cursed is one who lies with any animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends its list with a warning. Do not marry into the family of an עם הארץ. It uses strong, shocking comparisons to make the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words שקץ and שרץ are borrowed from the laws of forbidden creatures. They describe a home where Torah and מצוות are ignored. The פסוק about animals is applied to the daughters because, in this harsh rhetoric, a home with no Torah teaches no moral sense. The extreme language is meant to show how serious the concern is.

keyTerms.meaning: An ignoramus; one who does not learn or keep Torah carefully
An abomination; a forbidden, disgusting creature
A creeping creature (forbidden, and some types transmit טומאה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is deliberately exaggerated language from the חז"ל. It expresses how strongly they valued a Torah home. It is not a literal description of every person who lacks learning.

phrases.english: But he should not marry the daughter of ignoramuses,
because they are an abomination,
and their wives are like creeping creatures,
and about their daughters the verse says:
"Cursed is he who lies with any animal."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יִשָּׂא בַּת עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ladder by naming the family to avoid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should avoid marrying into the family of an עם הארץ.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has two sides. Seek a Torah family at almost any cost, and strongly avoid a family that rejects Torah.

steps.title: רבי: one who does not learn Torah may not eat meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads the פסוק 'זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף' as linking the right to eat meat with learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי says an ignoramus is forbidden to eat meat, as it says, 'This is the Torah of the animal and the bird.' Whoever engages in Torah may eat the meat of animals and birds. Whoever does not engage in Torah may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי makes a sharp statement about the עם הארץ. He supports it with a creative reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא simply sums up the laws of kosher animals: 'this is the law (תורה) of the animal and the bird.' רבי reads the word תורה as 'Torah learning.' So meat is tied to Torah, and only someone who learns may eat it. One explanation is that someone who doesn't learn won't know the laws of שחיטה and כשרות. Either way, this is a דרש making a moral point.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, editor of the משנה
'This is the law of the animal and the bird' (ויקרא י"א:מ"ו)
One who engages in Torah study

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:
An ignoramus is forbidden to eat meat (of an animal),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, בהמה ("animal").

phrases.english: as it is stated: "This is the law (Torah) of the animal and the bird":
Whoever engages in Torah
is permitted to eat the meat of animals and birds,
and whoever does not engage in Torah
is forbidden to eat the meat of animals and birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: עַם הָאָרֶץ אָסוּר לֶאֱכוֹל בְּשַׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the עם הארץ with another harsh statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using a דרש, eating meat is tied to engaging in Torah.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's extreme hyperbole about the עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר makes a shocking, exaggerated statement to express the depth of the conflict with hostile עמי הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is permitted to stab an ignoramus even on יום כיפור that falls on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר makes a deliberately shocking statement about the עם הארץ. It sets up a back-and-forth with his students in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking יום כיפור that falls on שבת, the holiest possible day, makes the statement even more extreme. That extremity is the signal that this is rhetoric, not law. The מפרשים explain that these statements target hostile people who hated and harmed Torah scholars. They are exaggeration meant to show how bitter the conflict was, and they were never meant to be acted on.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, student of רבי יוחנן
To stab him (kill without proper שחיטה)
יום כיפור that falls on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do NOT read this as real halacha. It is extreme hyperbole (גוזמא). Taking a life is absolutely forbidden. The statement shows the intensity of feeling against people who actively fought Torah, not a legal permission.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
An ignoramus, it is permitted to stab him
on יום כיפור that falls on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עַם הָאָרֶץ מוּתָּר לְנוֹחֳרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an even harsher statement in the same series about the עם הארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hyperbolic statement expressing extreme opposition to the hostile עם הארץ. It is not a practical ruling.

steps.title: The students ask about the wording
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי אלעזר why he said 'stab' instead of the gentler 'slaughter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, at least say 'to slaughter him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The students question the word רבי אלעזר chose. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחירה (stabbing) is a crude, improper killing. שחיטה is the proper, respectful method. The students suggest he could at least have used the more dignified word. Their question is about wording, not about whether the statement is true.

phrases.english: His students said to him:
Rebbi, say 'to slaughter him'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, אֱמוֹר לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the specific word used in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why use the harsh term 'stab' rather than 'slaughter'?

steps.title: Why 'stab' and not 'slaughter'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that שחיטה requires a ברכה and נחירה does not, so 'stab' fits his rhetoric better.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This (slaughtering) requires a blessing, and that (stabbing) does not require a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his students. He says the choice of 'stab' was on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Proper שחיטה is a מצווה act that comes with a ברכה, which gives it dignity. Stabbing has no ברכה. He chose the harsher word on purpose to keep the rhetoric sharp, so the whole exchange stays within the hyperbole.
steps.whatToRemember: These statements (רבי, רבי אלעזר) are intentional exaggerations. They express how seriously חז"ל viewed people who rejected and opposed Torah. They are not halachic rulings.

phrases.english: He said to them:
This (slaughtering) requires a blessing,
and that (stabbing) does not require a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: זֶה טָעוּן בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'stab' was chosen because שחיטה carries a ברכה and dignity, while stabbing does not.

steps.title: Do not travel on the road with an ignoramus
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that one may not travel together with an עם הארץ. He supports this from the פסוק calling Torah 'your life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is forbidden to accompany an עם הארץ on the road. The פסוק says about Torah, 'For it is your life and the length of your days.' Someone who does not learn Torah does not care about his own life. All the more so, he will not care about his fellow's life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a new rule: do not travel together with an עם הארץ, because he may be dangerous to you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says Torah is 'your life.' So a person who ignores Torah is ignoring his own life. If he does not protect his own life, he certainly will not protect yours. This is a קל וחומר from his own life to someone else's life.

keyTerms.meaning: To accompany or travel together with
Is it not all the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: עַם הָאָרֶץ אָסוּר לְהִתְלַוּוֹת עִמּוֹ בַּדֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: an ignoramus — it is forbidden to accompany him on the road,
as it is stated:
"For it is your life and the length of your days" (Devarim 30:20),
he has no pity on his own life (since he does not learn Torah),

phrases.aramaic: עַל חַיֵּי חֲבֵירוֹ — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן.
phrases.english: on his fellow's life — all the more so (he has no pity).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עַם הָאָרֶץ אָסוּר לְהִתְלַוּוֹת עִמּוֹ בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another statement from רבי אלעזר in the same series about the dangers of the עם הארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not travel together with an עם הארץ. Someone who does not value his own life (Torah) will not value another's.

steps.title: Tearing an ignoramus like a fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יוחנן, makes a shocking statement: it is 'permitted' to tear an עם הארץ like a fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is permitted to tear open an עם הארץ like a fish.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds an extreme, exaggerated statement to the series about the עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי אלעזר's 'stab him' statement earlier, this is strong rhetoric. It expresses how bitter the conflict was with hostile עמי הארץ. It is not a working legal permission. A fish needs no שחיטה at all, which makes the image even harsher.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a fish (which needs no שחיטה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as practical הלכה. The מפרשים explain these statements as exaggeration aimed at people who were openly hostile and dangerous to תלמידי חכמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
an ignoramus — it is permitted to tear him open like a fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of harsh statements about the עם הארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hyperbolic statement: an עם הארץ may be 'torn like a fish.'

steps.title: And from his back
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר יצחק adds one word to the previous statement: tear him 'from his back.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר יצחק said: And from his back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר יצחק builds on רבי יוחנן's statement by adding a detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing from the back cuts the spine, which kills immediately. Tearing from the belly does not. So this addition makes the exaggeration even sharper. It does not create a new idea. It intensifies the one before it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who adds to the previous statement

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
And (one may tear him) from his back.
phrases.notes: Cutting through the spine causes immediate death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: וּמִגַּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A direct addition to the previous step's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adds 'from his back' to the image of tearing like a fish.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's confession about his past hatred
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא. He admits that when he was an עם הארץ, he wished he could bite a תלמיד חכם like a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי עקיבא said: When I was an עם הארץ, I used to say, 'If only someone would give me a תלמיד חכם, and I would bite him like a donkey!'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the hostility is shown from the other side. רבי עקיבא, who started out as an עם הארץ, describes how much he once hated תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives an inside witness to the hatred described in the earlier statements. The conflict went both ways. The image of a donkey bite sets up the students' question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Who will give me / if only I had
And I would bite him like a donkey

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי עקיבא became one of the greatest תנאים. His story shows how far a person can grow, and it shows that the hatred was real.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Akiva said:
When I was an ignoramus, I said:
Who will give me a Torah scholar
and I will bite him like a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from scholars' statements about עמי הארץ to an עם הארץ's feelings about scholars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עם הארץ's hatred of תלמידי חכמים was so strong that רבי עקיבא once wished to bite one like a donkey.

steps.title: The students ask: why not say 'like a dog'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's students suggest that 'like a dog' would be the more natural way to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, say 'like a dog!'
steps.whatsHappening: The students question רבי עקיבא's wording. Dogs are the animals known for biting, so why mention a donkey? This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about word choice, not about the idea itself. It follows the same pattern as the students' question to רבי אלעזר about 'stab' versus 'slaughter' in step 6.

phrases.english: His students said to him:
Master, say (you would bite him) like a dog!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, אֱמוֹר כְּכֶלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבי עקיבא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי עקיבא compare himself to a biting donkey rather than the more obvious biting dog?

steps.title: A donkey's bite breaks bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that a donkey's bite breaks bones and a dog's bite does not. So 'donkey' shows how great his hatred was.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This one (a donkey) bites and breaks the bone. That one (a dog) bites but does not break the bone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his students. He chose 'donkey' on purpose, because it describes a more damaging bite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dog's bite tears flesh. A donkey's powerful jaws crush bone. By choosing the donkey, רבי עקיבא shows that he wanted to do serious harm, not just cause pain. This matches step 7, where the harsher word was also chosen on purpose.

phrases.english: He said to them:
this one (a donkey) bites and breaks bone,
and that one (a dog) bites but does not break bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: זֶה נוֹשֵׁךְ וְשׁוֹבֵר עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question about the wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Donkey' was chosen because its bite breaks bones, which expresses a deeper hatred than a dog's bite.

steps.title: Marrying a daughter to an ignoramus is like placing her before a lion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר. Marrying one's daughter to an עם הארץ is like tying her up in front of a lion, because he treats her roughly and without shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say: Whoever marries off his daughter to an עם הארץ, it is as if he tied her up and placed her in front of a lion. Just as a lion pounces and eats without any shame, so too an עם הארץ strikes his wife and has relations with her without any shame.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר warns fathers not to marry their daughters to an עם הארץ, and he explains the warning with a comparison to a lion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison has two parts. A lion grabs its prey and eats, with no shame. An עם הארץ hits his wife and then is intimate with her without making peace first, also with no shame. The point is that without Torah, a person lacks the refinement and sensitivity a wife deserves.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries off his daughter

steps.whatToRemember: This whole section uses deliberately extreme language to describe the deep hostility between hostile עמי הארץ and תלמידי חכמים in that era. The main ideas: Torah gives a person a value for life and refinement in how he treats others, and a match with a Torah family is strongly preferred.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Meir would say:
anyone who marries off his daughter to an ignoramus,
it is as though he binds her and places her before a lion.
Just as a lion mauls and eats,
and has no shame —
so too an ignoramus strikes (his wife) and has relations (with her),
phrases.notes: Without first making peace with her.

phrases.english: and has no shame.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַמַּשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of marriage with an עם הארץ (compare step 3) with a new ברייתא from רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying one's daughter to an עם הארץ is like placing her bound before a lion, because he treats her harshly and without shame.

steps.title: Only business keeps them from killing us
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר: if Torah scholars did not need עמי הארץ for business, the עמי הארץ would kill them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says: If we did not need them for business, they would kill us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא about how much the עם הארץ hates the תלמיד חכם. This continues the series of statements from steps 10–14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says the hatred is so strong that only one thing holds it back: shared business interests. Both sides need to trade with each other, and that need keeps the peace.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for / were it not that
Business dealings, trade (literally: carrying and giving)

steps.confusionAlert: The עם הארץ in this sugya is not just someone who lacks learning. The commentators explain it as a person who is openly hostile to Torah and to those who learn it. Do not read these statements as describing every simple Jew.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If we did not need them
for business dealings,
they would kill us.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another statement to the series about the hatred between עמי הארץ and תלמידי חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hatred of עמי הארץ toward Torah scholars is so great that only mutual business needs prevent violence.

steps.title: Learning Torah in front of an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that learning Torah in front of an עם הארץ is like violating his betrothed bride in front of him. He learns this from reading מורשה as מאורסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Anyone who learns Torah in front of an עם הארץ is as if he had relations with his betrothed in front of him, as it says: 'משה commanded us the Torah, an inheritance (מורשה).' Do not read it as 'inheritance' (מורשה) but as 'betrothed' (מאורסה).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא now looks at the other side: how the תלמיד חכם can hurt the עם הארץ. He backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah belongs to every Jew, like a betrothed bride waiting to be joined. When a scholar shows off his learning in front of someone who cannot learn, it is like taking that man's bride in front of him, which causes deep shame and pain. This also helps explain why the עם הארץ feels such hatred.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
Do not read it as... (a דרש method that reads a word with different vowels)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the text of the פסוק is changed. The written word stays מורשה. The דרש only adds a second layer of meaning by reading it as מאורסה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה לִפְנֵי עַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: Anyone who engages in Torah in front of an ignoramus,
it is as if he had relations with his betrothed in front of him,
as it says: 'Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance.'
Do not read 'inheritance,' but rather 'betrothed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵא רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the עם הארץ's hatred to the תלמיד חכם's responsibility not to shame him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning Torah in front of an עם הארץ in a way that shames him is a severe wrong, compared to violating his betrothed in front of him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא is not one-sided. The scholar also carries responsibility for how he treats the עם הארץ.

steps.title: Their hatred is greater than the nations' hatred
steps.stepSummary: The hatred of עמי הארץ for a תלמיד חכם is greater than the hatred the nations have for ישראל, and their wives hate even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hatred that עמי הארץ have for a תלמיד חכם is greater than the hatred that the nations of the world have for ישראל, and their wives hate even more than they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now ranks levels of hatred to show how intense this conflict is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two levels are set out. First, the עמי הארץ hate more than the nations hate ישראל. Second, their wives hate even more than the men themselves.

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹלָה שִׂנְאָה שֶׁשּׂוֹנְאִין עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם
phrases.english: Greater is the hatred with which ignoramuses hate a Torah scholar

phrases.aramaic: יוֹתֵר מִשִּׂנְאָה שֶׁשּׂוֹנְאִין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: than the hatred with which the nations of the world hate Israel,
and their wives even more than them.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּדוֹלָה שִׂנְאָה שֶׁשּׂוֹנְאִין עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי חייא's teaching by measuring how strong the hatred is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עם הארץ's hatred of the scholar is greater than the nations' hatred of ישראל, and his wife's hatred is greater still.

steps.title: One who learned and quit hates most of all
steps.stepSummary: A תנא adds that a person who once learned Torah and then left it hates Torah scholars more than anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: One who learned and then left, more than all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A short teaching adds one more level to the ranking from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who hates most is not someone who never learned. It is someone who tasted Torah and walked away. Seeing scholars reminds him of what he gave up, so his resentment is the strongest of all.

phrases.english: It was taught: one who studied and left,
hates more than all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא שָׁנָה וּפֵירַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the top level to the ranking of hatred.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who learned Torah and abandoned it hates scholars more than anyone.

steps.title: Six practical rules about עמי הארץ
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists six rules: do not appoint them as witnesses, do not accept their testimony, do not tell them secrets, do not make them guardians over orphans or over charity funds, and do not travel with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Six things were said about עמי הארץ. We do not give them testimony to witness. We do not accept testimony from them. We do not reveal a secret to them. We do not appoint them as guardian over orphans. We do not appoint them as guardian over a charity fund. We do not travel with them on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from descriptions of hatred to practical rules for dealing with an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every rule comes from the same worry: an עם הארץ cannot be trusted. He may testify falsely, spill secrets, misuse money belonging to orphans or the community, or even become dangerous when alone with a scholar on the road. The first two rules are separate: one is about choosing him as a witness ahead of time, and the other is about accepting his testimony in court.

keyTerms.meaning: A guardian or steward appointed to manage property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the first two rules. אין מוסרין להן עדות means we do not pick them to witness an event or deal. אין מקבלין ממנו עדות means a court does not accept their testimony.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Six things were said about ignoramuses:
We do not entrust them with testimony.
And we do not accept testimony from him.
And we do not reveal a secret to them.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְמַנִּין אוֹתָן אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס עַל הַיְּתוֹמִים.
phrases.english: And we do not appoint them as guardian over orphans.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְמַנִּין אוֹתָן אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס עַל קוּפָּה שֶׁל צְדָקָה.
phrases.english: And we do not appoint them as guardian over a charity fund.
And we do not accompany them on the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from aggadic descriptions of hatred to practical halachic rules of caution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six restrictions apply to an עם הארץ, all based on a lack of trust: no witnessing, no accepted testimony, no secrets, no guardianship over orphans or charity, and no traveling together.

steps.title: Some say: we do not announce his lost item
steps.stepSummary: The יש אומרים add another rule: we do not even announce an עם הארץ's lost item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: We do not even announce his lost item.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion inside the ברייתא adds one more restriction to the list of six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who finds a lost item must announce it so the owner can get it back. The יש אומרים say this obligation does not apply to the lost item of an עם הארץ. The word אף ('even') shows that this rule goes further than the first six.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a differing or additional opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives six agreed-upon rules for dealing with an עם הארץ, all rooted in distrust. The יש אומרים add a seventh: no obligation to announce his lost item.

phrases.english: And some say:
We do not even announce his lost item.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף אֵין מַכְרִיזִין עַל אֲבֵידָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further restriction from another opinion to the ברייתא's list of six.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the יש אומרים, there is no obligation to announce an עם הארץ's lost item.

steps.title: What is the first opinion's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא requires announcing an עם הארץ's lost item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא, why does he disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning of the תנא קמא, who did not include the extra rule of the יש אומרים. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, the יש אומרים said we do not announce an עם הארץ's lost item. The תנא קמא left that rule out of his list. So the גמרא wants to know why he still requires us to return the item.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And the first tanna? (What is his reason?)
phrases.notes: A very short question, but it is a complete thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the opinion that disagrees with the יש אומרים of step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תנא קמא holds that an עם הארץ's lost item must still be announced.

steps.title: Righteous children may end up using it
steps.stepSummary: The עם הארץ may have righteous descendants who will inherit and use the property, as the פסוק in איוב says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes good offspring come out of him and eat it (enjoy the property), as it says: "He may prepare it, but the righteous will wear it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we return the item because righteous children may one day inherit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The property is not only his. It may end up with a צדיק who comes from him. The פסוק in איוב teaches that what a wicked person prepares can later be used by a righteous one. So returning the item is never a waste.

keyTerms.meaning: "He prepares, and the righteous wears" (איוב כ״ז:י״ז)

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא returns an עם הארץ's lost item because his property may pass to righteous descendants.

phrases.english: Sometimes there comes out from him
upstanding offspring, who will eat (enjoy) it,
phrases.notes: "Eat" here means benefit from or inherit the property.

phrases.english: as it is said: "He may prepare it, but the righteous shall wear it."

steps.triggerLanguage: זִמְנִין דְּנָפֵיק מִינֵּיהּ זַרְעָא מְעַלְּיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The property may be inherited and used by righteous descendants, so it must be returned.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: one who left Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about someone who left Jerusalem holding sacrificial meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And so too, one who left, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The side topic about עמי הארץ is finished, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes the line about someone who left Jerusalem holding קדשים meat. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that someone who leaves Jerusalem with קדשים meat must go back and burn it, just like with חמץ. רבי מאיר says this applies to a כביצה, and רבי יהודה says a כזית. The quote reminds us of this מחלוקת so the גמרא can examine it.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too, one who went out (of Jerusalem)
Sacrificial meat, which may not leave Jerusalem

phrases.english: And so too, one who left, etc.
phrases.notes: "וכו׳" means the rest of the line of the משנה is understood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁיָּצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עם הארץ discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who left Jerusalem with קדשים meat must return to burn it. According to רבי מאיר the amount is a כביצה; according to רבי יהודה it is a כזית.

steps.title: Contradiction from the laws of זימון
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה suggests that רבי מאיר requires a larger amount than רבי יהודה. In the משנה of זימון, the positions are the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי מאיר holds only a כביצה is significant, and רבי יהודה holds that even a כזית is significant? But a contradiction is raised: How much must one eat to be included in a זימון? A כזית. And רבי יהודה says: a כביצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first draws a conclusion from our משנה about what each תנא considers a "significant" amount. Then it challenges that conclusion with the משנה about זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going back to Jerusalem is a burden, so it is only required for an amount that counts as significant. That means רבי מאיר sees only a כביצה as significant, while רבי יהודה sees even a כזית as significant. But in the laws of זימון, the first opinion (generally רבי מאיר) counts a כזית, while רבי יהודה requires a כביצה, so their positions are reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a conclusion drawn from a source)
The volume of an olive (smaller than a כביצה)
And they cast them against each other: a contradiction between two sources
Join together for a זימון (the group invitation to say ברכת המזון)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is arguing about how much food you must eat in general. The point is that each תנא should be consistent about which amount counts as "significant," and the two משניות make them look inconsistent.

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Meir holds
that only an egg-bulk is significant,
and Rabbi Yehuda holds
that an olive-bulk is also significant?
And a contradiction is raised:
Up to how much (eaten) do they join for a zimmun?
Up to an olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: This is the unnamed opinion, which usually follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda says: up to an egg-bulk!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר כְּבֵיצָה הוּא דַּחֲשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 23 and contrasts it with a משנה about זימון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה in our משנה about returning to burn the meat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here רבי מאיר treats only a כביצה as significant, and רבי יהודה treats a כזית as significant. In the laws of זימון, רבי מאיר counts a כזית and רבי יהודה requires a כביצה, so each one contradicts himself.

steps.title: The opinions are reversed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that in one of the sources the names must be switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The opinions are reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן solves the contradiction by saying that the names in one of the two משניות are switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not try to explain away the contradiction with a distinction. Instead, he fixes the text: in one source, the opinion given to רבי מאיר really belongs to רבי יהודה, and the reverse. Once this is done, each תנא is consistent about what counts as significant.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are swapped, so the names should be reversed

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common type of answer in the גמרא. Instead of a logical distinction, the text itself is corrected by switching the names.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are reversed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מוּחְלֶפֶת הַשִּׁיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each תנא seemed to contradict himself about what amount is significant.
steps.terutzMaskana: In one source, the names of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are switched, so each holds a consistent view.

steps.title: אביי: Keep the names, because the two disputes have different bases
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects switching the names. He says the dispute about זימון is based on פסוקים, while the dispute in our משנה is based on logical reasoning, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Actually, do not switch the names. There, in זימון, they disagree about how to read verses. Here, in our משנה, they disagree about logical reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer from רבי יוחנן's. He says we do not need to switch any names, because the two disputes come from different sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction only works if both disputes come from the same general idea about which amount counts. אביי breaks that assumption. One dispute is about reading a פסוק, and the other is about logical comparison, so each תנא can reach a different amount in each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, do not reverse (the names of the opinions)
There (in the other source, the משנה of זימון)
They disagree about how to read verses

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not adding to רבי יוחנן's answer. He is replacing it. רבי יוחנן switches the names, while אביי keeps the names exactly as they appear.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. Two disputes look contradictory, but the contradiction disappears once we see that each one rests on a different kind of reasoning.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Actually, do not reverse (the names).
phrases.notes: This rejects רבי יוחנן's approach of switching the names.

phrases.english: There, they disagree about verses,
phrases.notes: "There" refers to the משנה about זימון.

phrases.english: here, they disagree about logical reasoning.
phrases.notes: "Here" refers to our משנה about חמץ and sacrificial meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the contradiction from step 24, instead of רבי יוחנן's name-switch in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the bases of the two disputes: one rests on פסוקים and the other on סברא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה reverse their amounts between the two משניות, one source must have the names switched.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names stay as written. Each dispute has a different basis, so the positions do not contradict each other.

steps.title: How the זימון dispute depends on reading the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the זימון dispute. רבי מאיר reads "you shall eat" as eating, which means a כזית, and "be satisfied" as drinking. רבי יהודה reads the two words together as eating that satisfies, which is a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they disagree about verses. רבי מאיר holds that "And you shall eat" means eating, and "and be satisfied" means drinking. Eating is defined as a כזית. רבי יהודה holds that "And you shall eat and be satisfied" means eating that satisfies. What amount is that? A כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of אביי's answer. It shows that the זימון dispute comes from how each תנא reads the פסוק "ואכלת ושבעת."
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר divides the פסוק into two parts. "ואכלת" is ordinary eating, which is a כזית, and "ושבעת" refers to drinking. רבי יהודה reads the words as one phrase, meaning eating that brings satisfaction, and that requires a כביצה. Their amounts for זימון therefore come straight from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: "And you shall eat and be satisfied" (דברים ח:י), the source for ברכת המזון
An olive's volume, the standard halachic amount for "eating"
An egg's volume, a larger amount than a כזית

phrases.english: There, they disagree about verses:
phrases.notes: The גמרא now explains the first half of אביי's statement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds: "And you shall eat" means eating,
"and be satisfied" means drinking,
and eating is with an olive's volume.
phrases.notes: So according to רבי מאיר, a כזית of food is enough for זימון.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: "And you shall eat and be satisfied" means
eating that includes satisfaction,
and what is that? An egg's volume.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בִּקְרָאֵי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of אביי's answer, that in זימון the dispute is about פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the source of each position on זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: For זימון, רבי מאיר requires a כזית and רבי יהודה requires a כביצה, based on how each one reads "ואכלת ושבעת."

steps.title: רבי מאיר compares returning sacrificial meat to its impurity
steps.stepSummary: In our משנה, the dispute is about reasoning. רבי מאיר holds that the duty to return sacrificial meat matches the amount for its טומאה. Since food becomes טמא only at a כביצה, the duty to return it also starts at a כביצה. The גמרא then begins רבי יהודה's view, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, they disagree about logical reasoning. רבי מאיר holds that returning the meat is like its impurity. Just as its impurity applies at a כביצה, so too the duty to return it applies at a כביצה. And רבי יהודה holds that returning it is…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second half of אביי's answer. It shows that in our משנה, רבי מאיר's amount comes from a logical comparison, not from a פסוק. The step stops in the middle of רבי יהודה's view, which finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר links two amounts. Food is only able to become טמא when it is a כביצה, so he says the duty to go back and burn the meat also starts at a כביצה. That is why רבי מאיר holds the larger amount here, even though he holds the smaller amount, a כזית, for זימון.

keyTerms.meaning: Its return, meaning the duty to go back to ירושלים to burn the sacrificial meat
Its impurity, meaning the minimum size at which food can become טמא
"Just as… so too…", a formula used to compare two cases

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר contradicts himself. For זימון he requires a כזית because of the פסוק. Here he requires a כביצה because of the comparison to טומאה. Each amount has its own separate source.

phrases.english: Here, they disagree about logical reasoning,
phrases.notes: The גמרא now explains the second half of אביי's statement.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Meir holds: its return is like its impurity.
Just as its impurity is at an egg's volume,
so too its return is at an egg's volume.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds: its return…
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בִּסְבָרָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of אביי's answer, that in our משנה the dispute is about סברא. It contrasts with the reading of the פסוק in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the amounts in our משנה come from a logical comparison, independent of the זימון פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר requires a כביצה for returning sacrificial meat because he compares it to the amount for טומאה. רבי יהודה's reasoning continues on the next amud.
